dimensions.assessment: Affects all domestic hemp farmers, manufacturers, wholesalers, retailers, consumers, state regulatory agencies, and Medicare Advantage beneficiaries.
dimensions.evidence: Each person, before commencing business as a manufacturer of hemp-derived cannabinoid products, or wholesaler of hemp-derived beverages... shall make application for the permit

dimensions.assessment: Imposes new federal permits, criminal/civil penalties, strict product standards, milligram limitations, mandatory 3-tiered distribution for beverages, and tax structures.
dimensions.evidence: A tax is hereby imposed on all hemp-derived beverages produced, and removed for consumption or sale, within the United States. The rate of such tax... shall be 5 cents on each milligram of tetrahydrocannabinol

dimensions.assessment: Establishes specific federal excise taxes, sales revenue taxes, trust funds, and highway fund withholdings for non-compliant states.
dimensions.evidence: There are hereby appropriated to the Trust Fund for Oversight of Hemp-derived Cannabinoid Products amounts equivalent to the taxes received in the Treasury under sections 5901A and 5901B.

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act, Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, Social Security Act, Internal Revenue Code, and Title 23 United States Code.
dimensions.evidence: To preserve lawful hemp commerce while protecting consumers from high-THC synthetic intoxicants, and for other purposes.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent federal tax, regulatory, permitting, and highway withholding systems.

summary: The Lawful Hemp Protection Act preserves lawful hemp commerce while protecting consumers, particularly children, from high-THC synthetic intoxicants and unsafe products. It updates the definition of hemp, establishes strict FDA oversight and labeling rules, sets federal taxes and a permit system for manufacturers and wholesalers through the Internal Revenue Code, creates a three-tiered distribution system for hemp-derived beverages, and ties federal highway funds to state enforcement of hemp-impaired driving rules.

affected_groups.effect: Prohibited from purchasing, possessing, or consuming hemp-derived cannabinoid products.
Required to obtain federal permits, keep inventories and records, comply with manufacturing and testing standards, and pay new federal excise and sales taxes.
affected_groups.group: Manufacturers and wholesalers of hemp products

affected_groups.effect: Provided with uniform labeling, child safety warnings, QR codes for testing results, and potential coverage of hemp products under Medicare Advantage for the chronically ill.
Must enforce zero-tolerance driving rules for hemp impairment under threat of highway fund withholding, while retaining authority to enact stricter local laws.

key_provisions: Redefines hemp to mean the plant Cannabis sativa L. with a total tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) concentration of not more than 1 percent on a dry weight basis, explicitly excluding synthetic or artificially modified cannabinoids like HHC, THC-O-acetate, and THCP.
Prohibits the sale or possession of hemp-derived cannabinoid products to anyone under 21 years of age, and bans products designed to look like they are marketed to children.

Imposes federal taxes on hemp-derived cannabinoid products, including 5 cents per milligram of THC for hemp-derived beverages and a 5 percent tax on other cannabinoid products and manufacturer sales revenue.
Establishes a mandatory three-tiered distribution system for hemp-derived beverages separating manufacturers, wholesalers, and retailers.
Permits coverage of hemp-derived cannabinoid products under Medicare Advantage special supplemental benefits for the chronically ill and via CMI model engagement incentives.
Requires states to adopt zero-tolerance impaired driving standards for hemp or face a 10 percent withholding of certain federal highway funds.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for total projected tax revenues or the precise cost of federal administrative implementation.
Specific details on the exact criteria the Secretary of Health and Human Services and the Secretary of the Treasury will use for all future regulatory exceptions.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Lawful Hemp Protection Act preserves lawful hemp commerce while protecting consumers, particularly children, from high-THC synthetic intoxicants and unsafe products. It updates the definition of hemp, establishes strict FDA oversight and labeling rules, sets federal taxes and a permit system for manufacturers and wholesalers through the Internal Revenue Code, creates a three-tiered distribution system for hemp-derived beverages, and ties federal highway funds to state enforcement of hemp-impaired driving rules.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a sweeping restructuring of the U.S. hemp industry, shifting from minimal federal regulation to comprehensive oversight by the FDA and the Department of the Treasury. It impacts commercial growers, manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and consumers nationwide by establishing rigorous product definitions, mandatory permitting, federal excise taxation, age limits, and strict highway safety enforcement.
